topic_summary: Analysis of the personhood boundary in abortion law: the contested determination of when moral and legal status begins, which defines who counts as a rights-bearer and victim in abortion regulation. This boundary is not a single constraint but a contested kernel that different jurisprudential, religious, and philosophical traditions read differently, producing structurally incompatible constraint regimes.

key_entities: Pregnant person (rights-bearer in all frameworks, scope contested)
State (authority claiming power to adjudicate personhood boundary)
Religious traditions (Catholic, Protestant, Jewish, Islamic - varied personhood doctrines)
Medical profession (viability determination, gestational age assessment)
Constitutional courts (Roe, Dobbs, international human rights tribunals)
key_tensions: Fetal moral status vs maternal autonomy (zero-sum in rights allocation)
Fixed textual interpretation vs evolving medical/social context (originalism vs living constitutionalism)
Religious authority vs secular legal authority (whose kernel grounds legitimacy)
key_mechanisms: Trimester framework (Roe): viability as state interest threshold, operationalizes gradual personhood acquisition
Gestational limits: statutory boundaries (6-week, 15-week, 24-week bans) operationalize discrete personhood readings
key_absences: Non-Western legal traditions (Islamic fiqh ensoulment doctrines, Confucian relational personhood)
Disability rights framework (prenatal diagnosis and selective termination as personhood boundary enforcement)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood boundary: the threshold at which an entity acquires moral and legal status sufficient to constrain others' liberty
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested across religious (scriptural interpretation), philosophical (metaphysical criteria), medical (viability/sentience), and legal (constitutional text/precedent) domains. Each tradition claims interpretive authority via different grounding.
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Capture (Pattern 3): multiple authority structures claim exclusive interpretive legitimacy over the same kernel, each absorbing drift through their own hermeneutic layer without acknowledging rival readings as legitimate

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at conception (fertilization)
readings.authority_grounding: Natural law philosophy, Catholic magisterium, scriptural interpretation (Psalm 139, Jeremiah 1:5)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at conception; abortion becomes homicide-equivalent; no gestational distinctions; high suppression of maternal autonomy claims; contraception that prevents implantation potentially prohibited

readings.commitment: Moral personhood begins at ensoulment (40-120 days post-conception in Islamic and historical Christian traditions)
readings.authority_grounding: Islamic fiqh (hadith-based), Thomistic philosophy, historical Christian doctrine pre-1869
readings.expected_structural_delta: Early-term abortion permissible; fetus enters victim set at ensoulment threshold; creates temporal window for maternal autonomy; authority structure requires scholarly interpretation of religious texts

readings.commitment: Legal personhood begins at viability (capacity for independent survival outside womb)
readings.authority_grounding: Roe v. Wade framework, medical-technological determination, state interest balancing
readings.expected_structural_delta: Pre-viability abortion protected; post-viability state may prohibit except for health; boundary shifts with medical technology (24 weeks in 1973, potentially earlier now); fetus enters victim set at viability; state becomes arbiter via medical expertise

readings.commitment: Legal personhood begins at birth (complete expulsion from mother's body)
readings.authority_grounding: Common law tradition, bodily autonomy philosophy, some secular legal systems
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus never enters victim set; pregnant person sole rights-bearer throughout gestation; no state interest in fetal life pre-birth; abortion unrestricted by personhood logic (other regulations possible)

readings.commitment: Moral status increases gradually across gestation; no discrete threshold
readings.authority_grounding: Philosophical consequentialism, feminist care ethics, some bioethics frameworks
readings.expected_structural_delta: Proportional balancing throughout pregnancy; early abortion easier to justify than late; no binary victim/non-victim classification; state interest increases with gestational age; difficult to operationalize in binary legal frameworks

axiom_contradictions.basis: Conception reading requires accepting fetal moral status as equivalent to born persons from fertilization; birth reading requires accepting that location (inside/outside womb) determines moral status. No coherent framework can hold both: either the fetus is a person with rights that constrain maternal liberty, or it is not and maternal autonomy is absolute.

Conception reading requires binary personhood (entity either is or is not a person); gradualist reading requires rejecting binary personhood in favor of scalar moral status. These are metaphysically incompatible: personhood cannot be both binary and scalar simultaneously.

Viability reading grounds personhood in technological capacity for independent survival (contingent, changes with medical advancement); conception reading grounds personhood in intrinsic biological status (necessary, unchanging). No framework can hold both: personhood is either intrinsic to the entity or contingent on external technological capacity.

axes.structural_delta: Fetus acquires full moral and legal status at conception, entering victim set immediately
axes.primary_observable: Legal regimes prohibiting abortion from conception; criminal penalties for abortion equivalent to homicide; contraception restrictions targeting post-fertilization mechanisms
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct constraint structure; highest extractiveness; generates complete prohibition regime

axes.structural_delta: Fetus acquires moral status at ensoulment threshold, creating temporal window for early abortion
axes.primary_observable: Islamic fiqh rulings permitting early abortion; historical Christian doctrine allowing abortion pre-quickening; gestational limits at 40-120 days in religious legal systems
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct temporal structure; coordination mechanism within religious authority; structurally independent from conception and viability readings

axes.human_readable: Viability Reading (Personhood at Independent Survival Capacity)
axes.structural_delta: Fetus acquires legal status when technologically capable of surviving outside womb
axes.primary_observable: Roe v. Wade trimester framework; state abortion bans with viability exceptions; medical determination of gestational age and survival probability
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with technology-contingent structure; feeds into drift axis; medical authority as beneficiary

axes.structural_delta: Fetus never enters victim set; pregnant person retains sole rights-bearer status throughout gestation
axes.primary_observable: Legal regimes with no gestational limits; abortion access throughout pregnancy; common law born-alive rule
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with maximal maternal autonomy; structurally opposite to conception reading; distinct observable (no gestational restrictions)

axes.human_readable: Gradualist Reading (Scalar Moral Status Across Gestation)
axes.structural_delta: Moral status increases continuously; no discrete threshold; proportional balancing required
axes.primary_observable: Bioethics frameworks using proportionality analysis; trimester-based regulatory schemes with increasing restrictions; philosophical literature rejecting binary personhood
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading with distinct metaphysical structure (scalar vs binary); difficult to operationalize but philosophically live position

axes.structural_delta: Viability threshold shifts earlier with neonatal technology advancement, expanding state prohibition power
axes.primary_observable: Historical viability threshold movement (28 weeks in 1973 to 22-24 weeks currently); NICU survival rate improvements; legal challenges based on updated viability data
axes.selection_reason: Distinct structural mechanism; downstream of viability reading; captures technology-driven constraint expansion; independent observable (NICU survival rates)

axes.human_readable: Federalism Allocation (State vs Federal Authority Over Personhood)
axes.structural_delta: Post-Dobbs allocation of personhood determination to state legislatures rather than federal constitutional protection
axes.primary_observable: State-level abortion bans post-Dobbs; interstate travel for abortion; state constitutional amendments; federal legislation attempts (Women's Health Protection Act)
axes.selection_reason: Distinct structural axis (authority allocation, not personhood threshold); independent observable (state vs federal law); high extractiveness post-Dobbs

axes.human_readable: Disability-Selective Termination (Prenatal Diagnosis as Personhood Enforcement)
axes.structural_delta: Prenatal genetic testing enables selective termination based on disability, operationalizing contested personhood criteria
axes.primary_observable: Down syndrome abortion rates post-diagnosis (67-85% in US); sex-selective abortion bans; disability rights advocacy against prenatal testing
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: distinct structural mechanism but lower centrality; captured partially through conception/birth readings' victim set definitions; omega material for disability rights intersection

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Prenatal testing enables disability-selective abortion, operationalizing personhood criteria
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Lower centrality; intersection of personhood boundary with disability rights; victim set partially captured by kernel readings; omega material for disability justice framework

omegas.description: Is the personhood boundary a stable kernel across legal traditions, or do different traditions contest different kernels (e.g., bodily autonomy vs fetal life as the primary kernel)? Current analysis assumes single contested kernel; alternative is multiple non-overlapping kernels.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Five kernel readings pass pairwise independence test (distinct observables, distinct authority structures, distinct victim sets). Two non-kernel axes (medical_technology_drift, federalism_allocation) pass independence test against kernel readings and each other. Disability-selective termination deferred due to lower centrality and partial capture by kernel readings. Omegas generated for non-Western traditions absence, historical quickening doctrine, sentience reading, and kernel stability question.
